EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:
This Zone Change request from CB Community Business to MUR Mixed Use Residential
Emphasishas been submitted in order tore-establish residential use of the property.The subject
property contains a house built inthe1950s, which was converted to an office use at some point
in the past.The potential buyer of the property is interested in using the house as aresidence,
which is not permitted in the CB district.
When this area was originally zoned, mixed-use zoning districts did not exist in Cheyenne.
Therefore, itwas necessary to pick either commercial or residential zoning for this area.Itwas
zoned B-2, General Business, which was changed to CB Commercial Business in 1988.
MUR zoning allows residential uses but not the more intense commercial uses allowed in the CB
district, and appears to meet the criteria of UD CSec.2.2.1.d.Therefore, staff supports the proposed
zonechange.
ZONE CHANGEDATA: Inreviewing, providing comments, and making recommendations and
decisions on a proposed Zone Change Request, the Staff, Planning Commission and City Council
shall use the following criteria:
PLAN CHEYENNE.The application is in accordance with the development policies andphysical
patterns identified in the Comprehensive Plan.
The proposed rezoning would further Plan Cheyenne Policy 2.1.a, which“aims to foster
stabilization and enhancement of the city's established and older core neighborhoods."
Maintaining the residences onthe subject property also is in line with Principle 2.5: The Cheyenne
area will continue to have affordable“workforce”housing throughout our community."
Page 3, Zone Change Request/UDC-13-00546, 311-Z
4:
SURROUNDING AREA.The application is compatible with nearby property, specifically considering
existing zoning，the Comprehensive Plan, and any other official plans and policies created under
the guidance of that plan for these areas.
The area is a mix of residences and businesses, with many of the buildings havingbeen constructed
in the1950s, according to County Assessor records.
There is a house on the adjacent to theproperty to west owned by the current owner ofthe subject
property and across the alley to the north is ahouse owned by the gas station owner at the corner.
Across 18th Street to the south is a single-family house.
ZONING.BASIC STANDARDS&UsES.The suitability of the subject property for development
according to the standards and uses of the existing zoning district, compared to the suitability of
the subject property for development according to the standards anduses ofthe proposed zoning
district;
As mentioned previously, the subject property contains a 1950s house, which is more suitable to
mixed-use or residential zoning than commercial zoning.The property's location on Logan, abusy
collector roadway, is undoubtedly what led toits original commercial zoning; however, the parcel
is only5,214 squarefeet, which is likely too smallfor commercial redevelopment potential.Most
of the parcels in thevicinity are toosmall for commercial redevelopment.In order to redevelop as
commercial, several parcels would have to be consolidated into one ownership and one parcel.
Allowed residential uses inthe MUB and MUR zones are identical, allowingfor detached, semi-
attached, attached, multi-dwelling buildings, as well as live/work and mixed-use buildings.The
CB district, on the other hand, does not allow any residential uses.CB zoning is more appropriate
for larger lots that can accommodate the greater setback and parking requirements.
STREETs&OPENSPACE.The abilityof the subject property and surrounding vicinity to be
developed according to the Subdivision Standards in Article4considering the proposed zoning;
Overall, the Transportation Network is well established in this area. The area is laid out in the
Original City grid pattern and provides good connectivity for a variety of transportation
alternatives.Logan Avenue is a two-lane collector roadwith a center turn-lane.East of Logan the
grid transitions to the north-south alignment rather than the offset, northwest-southeast alignment
of the Original City.There is a bus stop at the corner of the property on Logan Avenue and an
alley along thenorth property line.
Since the neighborhood is already developed this criterion isless applicable to this proposal than
others. The well connected street network already in place supports the mixed-use zoning.
ZONING, INTENT, APPLICABILITY&DESIGN OBJECTIVES.The ability of the application to support
the Intent and Applicability statements of the proposed zoning district, and achieve the Design
Objectives of any specific standards.
The existing residential use conforms to the intent and applicability of the proposed MUR zone,
and design standards are in place to assure compatibility with the surrounding neighborhood.

The Community Business district is not an appropriate zone district for the residences and business
that are along this corridor.Inappropriate zoning can stifle investment in these situations.Hence
this applicant has asked foramore appropriate designation toprovide more certainty for future
investment. In the absence of a comprehensive look at the zoning along this corridor individual
landowners areforced to pursue changes in zoning increment ally.
ZONING, FUTURE DEVELOPMENT.The ability of all potential future development to meet all
applicable standards for development in the proposed zoning district, including other development
options in the event that any specific development proposed in association with the application is
not executed after approval.
If the zone changeisnot approved, the property could continue tobeused as office space, though
parking is limited on-site.Other possible options might include a daycare with additional fencing
and a drop-off lane.If the house were demolished and a new structure built, possible new uses
might include a small veterinary kennel/clinic, medical office/clinic, or a small specialty retail
store.Again, the sizeofthe property greatly restricts these possibilities, but theyare allowed under
the current CB zoning.
